opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 27%, driven by higher development expenses for late-stage assets and early-stage research, plus a charge of about $75M to end the Verzenio prostate cancer program.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and the back office — up 12% on promotional efforts for ongoing and future launches and higher compensation costs.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, charged at once — $0.10 of the quarter's EPS.

follow100Note: Mounjaro and Zepbound together supplied $26.51 of every $100 Lilly took in — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $2,335M (EPS $2.58). The release reports figures to one decimal place; they are rounded to whole millions here.
oneTimers: Acquired in-process R&D of $111M ($0.10 of EPS), up from $105M a year ago. Lilly counts IPR&D in both its reported and its non-GAAP figures.

Research and development expenses included a charge of approximately $75M associated with terminating the Verzenio prostate cancer program — the Phase 3 CYCLONE-3 trial in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, stopped for futility after an interim analysis.
otherDetail: Net other income of $27M — $160.9M of net other income, including net gains on investments in equity securities, partly offset by $133.8M of net interest expense.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — revenue more than tripled on strong demand and higher realized prices in the U.S. as savings-card use fell, with volume limited by available supply.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot (tirzepatide), launched in the U.S. in November 2023 — already $517M a quarter.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — Verzenio ($1.1B, +40%), Trulicity ($1.5B, -26%), Jardiance, Taltz and Humalog. Up 1% overall as Verzenio and Jardiance growth offset the Trulicity decline.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($1.8B, +218%) and Zepbound ($517M, launched November 2023) together brought in $2.3B of the $8.8B total — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide. Demand outpaced supply, and Lilly said sales growth for its incretin medicines will mainly depend on how much it can produce and ship.
takeaways.title: Two shots are 27% of revenue

takeaways.text: Lilly lifted full-year 2024 revenue guidance by $2.0B to $42.4–$43.6B, and reported EPS guidance by $1.25 to $13.05–$13.55, on the strength of Mounjaro and Zepbound and greater visibility into its production expansion for the rest of the year.
takeaways.title: Guidance raised by $2B

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 4.3 points to 80.9% on higher realized prices — mainly Mounjaro in the U.S. as savings-card dynamics faded — a favorable product mix, and, to a lesser extent, improvements in the cost of production. Operating income rose 68% to $2.5B.
takeaways.title: Margins widened as prices rose

verdict: Lilly's revenue rose 26% to $8.8B as Mounjaro more than tripled to $1.8B and Zepbound added $517M — and profit jumped 67% to $2.24B, prompting Lilly to raise full-year revenue guidance by $2B.
